evidence.note: Added a -S flag to its own compiler to emit and inspect assembly, then read the emitted asm for 00106.c to find codegen bugs (empty symbol names, %%rax double-percent escaping) — deliberately built verification infrastructure to inspect generated assembly.
Compiled 00111.c to asm with -S and ran `gcc -c t111.s` to confirm it assembles; isolated a register-width bug (movzwl into %ax vs %eax). Verifying compile success at instruction granularity.

Generated asm for 00014.c (p[0]=0 lvalue subscript), diagnosed that glv() used the pointer's storage address instead of its value, fixed only the write path — root-cause isolation via asm inspection, verifying runtime exit code.
Ran c-testsuite-only subset for faster signal than the full 780 suite, and used python scripts to categorize failures by type (43 compile fails, 92 runtime fails) to prioritize fixes.
Checked the Assign codegen handler, identified chained-assignment bug (movq %rcx,%rax lost in a rewrite), fixed and re-verified on 00011.c specifically before re-running the suite.

reasoning: The agent built a deliberate verification loop: it invested in a -S flag to inspect emitted assembly, used `gcc -c` to isolate assembly-syntax failures from runtime failures, verified both compile success and runtime exit codes on individual small test cases, ran quicker per-suite subsets, and categorized failures by root-cause type — matching the level-8 anchor closely. It falls short of 10 because it reused existing tiny test files rather than authoring minimal repros, had no reusable bisect harness or systematic asm diffing, and didn't probe edge semantics (overflow/promotion) with targeted cases; the loop was also frequently disrupted by fragile edits.
